Friction drag and pressure drag both hin: In sports engineering both types of drag are important depending on the application. Sports like baseball and golf, reduce pressure drag as it is more important than friction due to the high speeds and flow seperation around the ball. The added stitches on a baseball or the dimples on a golf ball help improve the transition between laminar and turbulent boundary layers. However, a sport like swimming tends to reduce friction drag as it helps decrease resistance along the body surface. This can help the swimmer maintain higher speeds and reduce energy loss caused by friction drag.
Laminar flow over a flat plate provides: An example of a system where low drag is prioritized over max heat transfer is in Shinkansen high speed train or bullet trains. Shinkansen's are designed to have streamlined shapes to minimize aerodynamic drag and noise when traveling at high speeds. If there is an increase in turbulence the train would have an increase in energy consumption and create unwanted noise which is not ideal in high populated areas. So, cooling systems for onboard electronics and mechanical components are designed to be internal and not have major impacts on external airflow. This minimize convective heat transfer, but keeps the smooth / streamlined airflow over the train.

How could optimizing the heat transfer a: Optimizing the heat transfer across large scale tube banks like those in power plant condensers or heat exchangers can help society both economically and environmentally. When the heat transfer is optimized the system can use less energy which reduces fuel for the plant which can be directed towards the consumer with reduced energy prices. Furthermore, with more optimized heat transfer the local water temperatures would be cooler as the power plant can reduce the amount of heat discharged to nearby water used for cooling. By reducing the heat in the water the aquatic life in the water do not have to worry about harmful pollution.
